claims.text: This trip was sold on an upfront quote. The fare_breakdown records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd non-null at SGD 28.00, so the price was fixed at booking and POL-RD-02's distance-and-time recomputation does not run at all; POL-RD-11 is the clause that governs the rider's remedy on this trip.

The ledger then charged SGD 67.50 against that SGD 28.00 quote, which is SGD 39.50 more than the upfront price the platform itself set. The charge was assembled from distance (SGD 16.40) and time (SGD 40.50) lines that the upfront contract had already fixed at booking, plus a SGD 6.00 airport surcharge and a SGD 0.80 platform fee. The rider disputes exactly that excess over the quote, and POL-RD-11(a) makes it refundable in full.

POL-RD-11(a) fixes the refund as charged_total less quoted_fare less the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The only properly chargeable line here is the SGD 6.00 Changi airport surcharge, because this trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport Terminal 3 (trip_record pickup label 'Changi Airport Terminal 3, Departure Level Door 5'). There are no ERP gantry lines (erp_gantries is empty), no tolls, and a SGD 0.00 waiting-time fee. The refund is therefore 67.50 − 28.00 − 6.00 = SGD 33.50, already a multiple of SGD 0.05.

The entitlement under POL-RD-11(a) is arithmetic on the fare ledger against the price the platform quoted, and it does not depend on establishing a POL-RD-01 deviation. Even if no distance deviation is established on this trip, the rider still recovers the amount by which the platform charged above its own fixed upfront price; POL-RD-11 supplies that remedy and POL-RD-01's threshold test does not displace it.

Nothing on the record reduces that figure as a rider-caused detour. The trip's chat_log is empty — message_count 0, messages array empty — so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction exoneration is unavailable: there is no rider message asking for a stop, a waypoint or a particular road, and no waypoint_hint to corroborate one. The driver cannot point to a recorded instruction to justify any part of the charge.

No external traffic cause is on file either. The traffic_advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00517-01 is MISSING — its payload is null and its weight_multiplier is 0.0 — so POL-RD-03's comparison (an advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, with an overlapping validity window, matched by a route that leaves and rejoins the corridor) cannot be run on this record, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and any 'something external happened' explanation carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The absence is itself citable, and it leaves the POL-RD-11(a) arithmetic untouched.

The rider carries no special corroboration burden. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so POL-RD-08's condition (4 or more claims in 60 days with 1 or fewer substantiated) does not attach and no corroboration beyond the artifacts already cited is required of this rider.

The driver's own account confirms the charge was not the product of any route the rider chose. He states the app crashed mid-trip, that he dropped the rider at the hotel, and that the app 'completed the trip by itself' — 'I didn't choose the amount.' The trip_record corroborates the shape of that account: status COMPLETED, a post-hoc charge at 22:42:00, and zero chat messages. Nothing on the rider's side explains the SGD 39.50 jump from quote to charge, which is precisely why POL-RD-11(a) places that excess back with the rider.

The driver-device trace is IMPAIRED, and I disclose that: EV-GPS-00517 carries weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP (a single 620-second gap from 22:26:30 to 22:36:50) and LOW_COVERAGE (65.6% across the active window). That is exactly the frozen-icon failure the rider describes — the app stopped reporting mid-trip. A telemetry failure on the platform's own side is not the rider's to pay for, and it does not disturb the POL-RD-11(a) figure, which is computed from the fare ledger and the quoted fare and not from the trace.

No route deviation is established on this trip's own numbers. The trace-derived excess over the 19.6 km optimal route is 0.3 km and 1.53%. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH an excess greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms; neither limb is met, so no deviation exists and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION on the deviation however the rider characterises the trip. Disclosure: the trace artifact is impaired — issue codes GPS_GAP (one 620-second gap) and LOW_COVERAGE (65.6%), weight_multiplier 0.39 — and even on the straight-line-between-bounding-fixes reading POL-RD-07(i) prescribes across the gap, an excess of this size is nowhere near the 0.8 km gate.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured either from an unimpaired trace or from one of the independent sources POL-RD-07(ii) names. She can show neither: the measured excess is 0.3 km / 1.53%, and the only trace on file is impaired at weight 0.39. The deviation claim therefore fails at the first limb of POL-RD-08 before any exculpatory clause is reached.

This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip — fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 28.00 — so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02 does not run. The distance and time charges were fixed at booking, no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however the trip unfolded, and her remedy is confined to the POL-RD-11(a) arithmetic and any POL-RD-09 pass-through correction. The driver's unrecovered cost on any detour is not recoverable from the rider under this clause.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern, so no uplift and no referral lies against the driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 — far below both POL-RD-06 tests (3 or more flags, or a 0.05 ratio with at least 40 trips). Neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) nor the driver-conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) is available on these figures.

The trace is impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a): a single gap of 620 seconds between consecutive fixes, from 22:26:30 to 22:36:50, far beyond the 90-second limb, spanning a 6.89 km straight-line jump. POL-RD-07(ii) then bars establishing anything on the trace alone and demands an independent source; there is none — the chat log holds 0 messages, no ERP gantry was charged, and the driver's statement admits no route. POL-RD-10(3) therefore makes escalation mandatory and the disputed amount is held rather than refunded. Disclosure: EV-GPS-00517 is impaired with issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE at weight_multiplier 0.39.

Under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence in any finding carried by the trace is capped by its weight_multiplier of 0.39, which is below the 0.70 platform-wide escalation floor in POL-RD-10(1). The route question here rests on EV-GPS-00517 alone, so the cap bites and the case escalates automatically; the bundle mean weight is context only and is not the cap.

If the judge reaches the POL-RD-11(a) arithmetic, the only properly chargeable pass-through on this trip is the Changi Airport surcharge, because the trip originates at Terminal 3. That trip ran at 22:05 SGT on Saturday 5 September 2026, inside the Friday/Saturday/Sunday 17:00-23:59 peak window the fare model sets, so the properly chargeable surcharge is SGD 8.00 and not the SGD 6.00 itemised. The refundable excess would then be 67.50 less 28.00 less 8.00, i.e. SGD 31.50, not SGD 33.50.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you agree on the shape of this trip, and the fare ledger decides it. The trip was sold on an upfront quote: EV-FARE-00517 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of SGD 28.00, so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02's distance-and-time recomputation does not run at all. Both advocates are right on that point, and the rider's remedy is confined to the POL-RD-11(a) arithmetic and any POL-RD-09 pass-through correction.

On the route question: the driver-device trace EV-GPS-00517 is impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) and is disclosed as such - issue codes GPS_GAP (a single 620-second gap, 22:26:30 to 22:36:50) and LOW_COVERAGE (65.6% across the active window), weight_multiplier 0.39. Its own derived reading is an excess of 0.3 km / 1.53%, far below the POL-RD-01 gate of 0.8 km and 20%; read as recorded or straight-lined across the gap under POL-RD-07(i), no deviation is established. Nothing in this ruling turns on that, however.

The driver's argument that POL-RD-10(3) forces escalation is rejected. POL-RD-10(3) and POL-RD-07(iii) exist so that a deviation is not established on an impaired trace that has no independent corroboration - they presuppose that a deviation finding is at issue. Here none is: the rider's entitlement under POL-RD-11(a) is arithmetic on the fare ledger against the price the platform itself quoted, and it does not rest on the trace. There is no data failure to escalate, and the case is decidable. The trace's impairment is named and discounted, but because the deciding figures are carried by EV-FARE-00517 (weight 1.0) and EV-TRIP-00517 (weight 1.0) - not by the trace - it does not lower the confidence of this ruling.

The arithmetic under POL-RD-11(a): the charged total was SGD 67.50 (EV-FARE-00517); the quoted fare was SGD 28.00; the only properly chargeable pass-through is the Changi Airport surcharge. The trip originates at Changi Airport Terminal 3 (EV-TRIP-00517 pickup label 'Changi Airport Terminal 3, Departure Level Door 5'), and it ran at 22:05 SGT on Saturday 5 September 2026, inside the fare model's Friday/Saturday/Sunday 17:00-23:59 peak window, so the properly chargeable surcharge is SGD 8.00, not the SGD 6.00 itemised. There are no ERP or toll lines (erp_gantries is empty) and the waiting-time fee is SGD 0.00. The refund is therefore 67.50 - 28.00 - 8.00 = SGD 31.50. The rider's figure of SGD 33.50 uses the SGD 6.00 itemised surcharge and understates the properly chargeable one; the driver's figure of SGD 31.50 is the correct one.

The rider is right, though it changes nothing, that no rider-requested detour reduces the figure (the chat_log EV-CHAT-00517 holds no messages, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable), and that no special corroboration burden attaches to her (rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0). No repeat-deviation pattern arises on the driver's profile (deviation_flags_90d 0 over completed_trips_90d 250), so there is no POL-RD-06 uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) referral; and because the airport surcharge sits on a trip that does originate at Changi and no gantry line was charged, no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral fires. The driver's own account - that the app crashed, that he dropped the rider at the hotel, that the app completed the trip by itself and he did not choose the amount - is consistent with the ledger and the rider's account and supports the finding that the charge was not for a route the rider chose.

Outcome: of the SGD 67.50 charged, SGD 31.50 is refunded to the rider; the SGD 28.00 quoted fare and the properly chargeable SGD 8.00 airport surcharge stand.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider first. You were charged far more than the price you agreed to, and most of the difference comes back to you. The trip was sold on an upfront quote: the fare ledger EV-FARE-00517 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 28.00. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time lines were fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02's metre recomputation does not run and no route-deviation refund is available however the trip unfolded. What is left is the arithmetic. You were charged 67.50 (charged_total), which is 39.50 above the platform's own quoted price. POL-RD-11(a) refunds that excess less the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The only such line is the Changi Airport surcharge, because the trip originated at Changi Terminal 3. The trip left at 22:05 SGT on Saturday 5 September 2026, inside the fare model's Friday-Sunday 17:00-23:59 peak window, so the properly chargeable surcharge is the peak rate SGD 8.00, not the SGD 6.00 itemised. Because 8.00 is a genuine pass-through that the rider properly owes, the refund is 67.50 - 28.00 - 8.00 = SGD 31.50. That is a PARTIAL_REFUND: the quoted fare (28.00) and the properly chargeable surcharge (8.00) stand, and the rider recovers the rest.

To the driver. Your request to escalate the whole case is refused. The driver-device trace EV-GPS-00517 is indeed impaired - weight_multiplier 0.39, issue codes GPS_GAP (one 620-second gap, 22:26:30 to 22:36:50) and LOW_COVERAGE (65.6%) - and I disclose it, but it decides nothing here. The refund is arithmetic on the fare ledger EV-FARE-00517 (weight 1.0), not on the trace, and on an upfront-quote trip no deviation finding is needed at all. POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) govern whether a route deviation can be established on an impaired trace; with no deviation to establish they are not engaged, so the trace's weight does not cap this ruling below the 0.70 floor and does not force escalation.

Your account (the app crashed, "I didn't choose the amount") is accepted. It explains the telemetry gap and confirms the amount was not chosen by the rider, but it does not let you keep a metered over-run on a price that was fixed at booking. Your other point - that no deviation is established, the trace excess being 0.3 km / 1.53%, below both POL-RD-01 gates - is correct but immaterial under POL-RD-11, which makes no distance refund available either way. There is no repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days), so no POL-RD-06(b) uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. The chat log EV-CHAT-00517 is empty, so no rider-requested detour arises under POL-RD-04, and the rider's profile carries no special corroboration burden under POL-RD-08. No ERP gantry and no surcharge line is a billing defect (the trip did originate at the airport), so no POL-RD-09(4) referral. No referral is issued and no driver compensation is due.

One question I leave with the platform rather than in referrals: why its system charged 39.50 above its own fixed upfront quote on a trip where, on the driver's own account, the app completed itself.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this trip was sold on an upfront quote, and that is what decides it.

EV-FARE-00517 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd SGD 28.00, and the ledger charged total_charged SGD 67.50 - SGD 39.50 more than the platform's own fixed price. Under POL-RD-11(a) the rider's remedy is the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. On this record the only such line is the SGD 6.00 Changi Airport surcharge: the trip originated at Changi Terminal 3, erp_gantries is empty, there are no tolls, and the waiting-time fee is SGD 0.00. The refund is therefore 67.50 - 28.00 - 6.00 = SGD 33.50. Payment status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so this is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 33.50; the rider keeps the SGD 34.00 that represents the quote plus the properly chargeable surcharge. POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront trip, so no distance-or-time recomputation is performed.

On the route itself, the trace measures an excess of 0.3 km / 1.53% over the 19.6 km optimal, below both POL-RD-01 gates (0.8 km and 20%). No deviation is established, and on an upfront trip that would make no difference to the money either way.

On the GPS trace the driver is right about the facts and wrong about the consequence. EV-GPS-00517 is impaired - GPS_GAP (one 620-second gap, 22:26:30-22:36:50) and LOW_COVERAGE (65.6%) - at weight_multiplier 0.39, and that impairment is disclosed and applied. It does not decide this case, because the refund is computed from the fare ledger (EV-FARE-00517), which is complete at weight 1.0, and POL-RD-11(a) is arithmetic on that ledger. The driver's escalation argument is rejected: POL-RD-07(ii)-(iii) and POL-RD-10(3) govern the establishment of a route deviation on a trace that cannot carry one; here the excess measures 0.3 km even on the POL-RD-07(i) straight-line reading most favourable to the driver, so there is no deviation to establish and no deviation finding resting on the trace. The rider's point that the telemetry failure does not disturb the POL-RD-11(a) figure is accepted.

The driver's alternative surcharge figure is also rejected. He asks me to read the SGD 8.00 peak surcharge from the fare model because the trip began at 22:05 on a Saturday. The record's own money block itemises the airport surcharge at SGD 6.00 under this trip's rate card (RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDEX), which the trip record carries, and computes the properly chargeable figure and the POL-RD-11(a) remedy at SGD 33.50. The refund is SGD 33.50, not SGD 31.50.

Claims accepted but not moving the money: the chat log is empty, so there is no rider-requested detour to credit under POL-RD-04; the rider carries no special corroboration burden (deviation_claims_60d 0, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0), so POL-RD-08 attaches no extra requirement; there is no repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 of 250 completed trips), so neither the POL-RD-06(b) uplift nor the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral fires; the driver's own account (app crashed, trip completed by itself, 'I didn't choose the amount') is consistent with the ledger error but adds nothing to the arithmetic. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00517-01, weight 0.0) is not relied on by either party - nobody asserts a traffic cause - so POL-RD-03 is not in play and the absence is a gap in the bundle, not a ground of decision. No phantom gantry or wrongly applied surcharge appears, so POL-RD-09(4) produces no billing-integrity referral either.

Confidence 0.90, within the cap of 1.0 set by EV-FARE-00517, the artifact carrying the deciding fact.

ruling.explanation: Addressed to both of you. This was an upfront-quoted trip, so the fare is fixed and the route question does not drive the money. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-00517) records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 28.00, so POL-RD-11 governs and POL-RD-02's distance-and-time recomputation does not run: on a fixed-price trip a detour costs the rider nothing on those lines. The remedy is POL-RD-11(a): the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quoted fare plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The ledger charged SGD 67.50. Deduct the SGD 28.00 quote and the one properly chargeable line, the Changi Airport surcharge: this trip ORIGINATED at Changi Terminal 3 (EV-TRIP-00517, pickup 'Changi Airport Terminal 3, Departure Level Door 5') at 22:05 on Saturday 5 September 2026, inside the fare model's peak window (Friday/Saturday/Sunday 17:00-23:59 SGT), so the properly chargeable surcharge is the peak SGD 8.00 and not the SGD 6.00 itemised on the ledger. There are no ERP or toll lines (erp_gantries empty) and the waiting-time fee is SGD 0.00. The refund is 67.50 - 28.00 - 8.00 = SGD 31.50, already a multiple of SGD 0.05. The rider's claim of SGD 33.50 is accepted in method but rejected on the surcharge figure, because it deducts only the off-peak SGD 6.00. Nothing reduces the figure as a rider-caused detour: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00517) holds zero messages and no waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable and the driver cannot point to any recorded instruction. The driver's point that no route deviation is established (excess 0.3 km and 1.53%, under both POL-RD-01 gates) is accepted, but it decides nothing here, because the POL-RD-11(a) refund does not depend on a deviation finding in either direction. Escalation is refused. The GPS trace is impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) - one 620-second gap from 22:26:30 to 22:36:50, a 6.89 km straight-line jump - and I disclose that the artifact EV-GPS-00517 carries weight_multiplier 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP and LOW_COVERAGE. But POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) control the establishment of a route deviation from a trace; no deviation finding is needed or made, so the impairment cannot make this case undecidable. The deciding facts - charged_total, quoted_fare, the surcharge and the airport origin - are carried by EV-FARE-00517 and EV-TRIP-00517, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and POL-RD-10(1) is not engaged. The driver's own account (app crashed mid-trip, trip completed by itself, 'I didn't choose the amount') is consistent with the ledger overcharge and is not contested. Finally, there is no repeat-deviation pattern to answer: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days, so neither the POL-RD-06(b) uplift nor a POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available. Referrals: none. No POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral either, because there are no ERP lines and the surcharge is on a trip that originates at Changi.

ledger.claim: This trip was sold on an upfront quote. The fare_breakdown records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd non-null at SGD 28.00, so the price was fixed at booking and POL-RD-02's distance-and-time recomputation does not run at all; POL-RD-11 is the clause that governs the rider's remedy on this trip.

The ledger then charged SGD 67.50 against that SGD 28.00 quote, which is SGD 39.50 more than the upfront price the platform itself set. The charge was assembled from distance (SGD 16.40) and time (SGD 40.50) lines that the upfront contract had already fixed at booking, plus a SGD 6.00 airport surcharge and a SGD 0.80 platform fee. The rider disputes exactly that excess over the quote, and POL-RD-11(a) makes it refundable in full.

POL-RD-11(a) fixes the refund as charged_total less quoted_fare less the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. The only properly chargeable line here is the SGD 6.00 Changi airport surcharge, because this trip ORIGINATES at Changi Airport Terminal 3 (trip_record pickup label 'Changi Airport Terminal 3, Departure Level Door 5'). There are no ERP gantry lines (erp_gantries is empty), no tolls, and a SGD 0.00 waiting-time fee. The refund is therefore 67.50 − 28.00 − 6.00 = SGD 33.50, already a multiple of SGD 0.05.

The entitlement under POL-RD-11(a) is arithmetic on the fare ledger against the price the platform quoted, and it does not depend on establishing a POL-RD-01 deviation. Even if no distance deviation is established on this trip, the rider still recovers the amount by which the platform charged above its own fixed upfront price; POL-RD-11 supplies that remedy and POL-RD-01's threshold test does not displace it.

Nothing on the record reduces that figure as a rider-caused detour. The trip's chat_log is empty — message_count 0, messages array empty — so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction exoneration is unavailable: there is no rider message asking for a stop, a waypoint or a particular road, and no waypoint_hint to corroborate one. The driver cannot point to a recorded instruction to justify any part of the charge.

No external traffic cause is on file either. The traffic_advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00517-01 is MISSING — its payload is null and its weight_multiplier is 0.0 — so POL-RD-03's comparison (an advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, with an overlapping validity window, matched by a route that leaves and rejoins the corridor) cannot be run on this record, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and any 'something external happened' explanation carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The absence is itself citable, and it leaves the POL-RD-11(a) arithmetic untouched.

ledger.claim: The rider carries no special corroboration burden. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so POL-RD-08's condition (4 or more claims in 60 days with 1 or fewer substantiated) does not attach and no corroboration beyond the artifacts already cited is required of this rider.

The driver's own account confirms the charge was not the product of any route the rider chose. He states the app crashed mid-trip, that he dropped the rider at the hotel, and that the app 'completed the trip by itself' — 'I didn't choose the amount.' The trip_record corroborates the shape of that account: status COMPLETED, a post-hoc charge at 22:42:00, and zero chat messages. Nothing on the rider's side explains the SGD 39.50 jump from quote to charge, which is precisely why POL-RD-11(a) places that excess back with the rider.

The driver-device trace is IMPAIRED, and I disclose that: EV-GPS-00517 carries weight 0.39 with issue codes GPS_GAP (a single 620-second gap from 22:26:30 to 22:36:50) and LOW_COVERAGE (65.6% across the active window). That is exactly the frozen-icon failure the rider describes — the app stopped reporting mid-trip. A telemetry failure on the platform's own side is not the rider's to pay for, and it does not disturb the POL-RD-11(a) figure, which is computed from the fare ledger and the quoted fare and not from the trace.

No route deviation is established on this trip's own numbers. The trace-derived excess over the 19.6 km optimal route is 0.3 km and 1.53%. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH an excess greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms; neither limb is met, so no deviation exists and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION on the deviation however the rider characterises the trip. Disclosure: the trace artifact is impaired — issue codes GPS_GAP (one 620-second gap) and LOW_COVERAGE (65.6%), weight_multiplier 0.39 — and even on the straight-line-between-bounding-fixes reading POL-RD-07(i) prescribes across the gap, an excess of this size is nowhere near the 0.8 km gate.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured either from an unimpaired trace or from one of the independent sources POL-RD-07(ii) names. She can show neither: the measured excess is 0.3 km / 1.53%, and the only trace on file is impaired at weight 0.39. The deviation claim therefore fails at the first limb of POL-RD-08 before any exculpatory clause is reached.

The distance and time charges were fixed at booking, no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however the trip unfolded, and her remedy is confined to the POL-RD-11(a) arithmetic and any POL-RD-09 pass-through correction. The driver's unrecovered cost on any detour is not recoverable from the rider under this clause.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern, so no uplift and no referral lies against the driver. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 — far below both POL-RD-06 tests (3 or more flags, or a 0.05 ratio with at least 40 trips). Neither the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) nor the driver-conduct referral in POL-RD-06(c) is available on these figures.

The trace is impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a): a single gap of 620 seconds between consecutive fixes, from 22:26:30 to 22:36:50, far beyond the 90-second limb, spanning a 6.89 km straight-line jump. POL-RD-07(ii) then bars establishing anything on the trace alone and demands an independent source; there is none — the chat log holds 0 messages, no ERP gantry was charged, and the driver's statement admits no route. POL-RD-10(3) therefore makes escalation mandatory and the disputed amount is held rather than refunded. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence in any finding carried by the trace is capped by its weight_multiplier of 0.39, which is below the 0.70 platform-wide escalation floor in POL-RD-10(1). The route question here rests on EV-GPS-00517 alone, so the cap bites and the case escalates automatically; the bundle mean weight is context only and is not the cap.
